coverage_notes: Roster frozen for historical research on 2026-11-08. It contains 50 new people, eight institutions, and source seeds.
Coverage follows direct White House AI roles, government-wide AI authorities, and the full publicly named October 2026 SIF roster. It includes relevant former officials who served from 2023 onward.
Membership source excerpts are deliberately short. The cited page supplies the surrounding membership context.

Official-role documents hosted by the American Presidency Project preserve government text. Academic, conference, and press biographies use source_type reporting where no direct government source was found.
Do not treat null role end dates as evidence of current service.
Seed URLs are research leads, not approved quotations. Notes distinguish direct statements, event routes, and institutional records. Duplicate mirrors should not count as independent evidence.
unresolved: No public SIF charter or official membership list was found; membership and advisory distinctions rely on cited reporting.
Wiles and Walters departure dates and continued SIF status need follow-up after the November 8, 2026 staff-change report.
Farmer's completed federal CIO appointment remains unconfirmed; Flagg's official source verifies only his deputy role.
No identifiable White House AI official named Lincoln was verified. MIT Lincoln Laboratory appears in Staheli's post-government affiliation.
A complete historical PCAST working-group membership review remains outside this staged core-official pass; the institutional profile and existing co-chair amendments cover the body.
No direct AI policy statement was found for Susie Wiles, Richard Walters, or Thomas Lind during this search. Their documented roles still support roster inclusion.
Carter Farmer and Thomas Flagg have role-only seeds. Klomp, Easter, Bonner, Zhu, and Walden need event transcripts before assigning personal positions.

coverage_notes: Verified on 2026-11-08 against retrieved official leadership pages, dated official documents, and clearly marked reporting. Historical status does not imply a current appointment. Dates remain null unless an exact effective date appears.
Research seeds identify promising source pages. They do not constitute verified personal quotations or policy judgments. Shared releases require attribution checks.
Current official nomenclature uses CAISSI and Super Intelligence. Historical AISI and CAISI roles retain the names that sources used.

Added Commerce and State agency AI leadership: Brian Epley, Amy Ritualo, and former State chief Matthew Graviss. Authored compliance plans are labeled institutional policy, not direct personal speech.

Seed counts are discovery URLs, not counts of independent statements. Hearing pages, transcripts, video, role biographies and authored policy plans can overlap. Deduplicate events and require direct attribution before extracting a personal position.
Current technical-role coverage remains useful even when public personal remarks are sparse. No absence of views is inferred from a failed search.
unresolved: No exact current employment dates are asserted for most roles. Current-page verification date does not establish an appointment date.
Ted Suzman's October 2026 official role is verified. Search did not locate three independent personally attributed public AI statement sources.
BIS lists its Deputy Under Secretary for Policy as vacant. Do not retain a prior incumbent as current without a later source.
Current leadership is established for Katherine Reid, Jessica Curyto, John Sonderman, Noah Jaffe and David Peters, but individual AI statement coverage needs further targeted research.
The most recent directly reviewed government role record for Helberg is February 2026 testimony, supplemented by October 2026 UAE government readouts.
Christiano's senior adviser role uses September 2026 reporting. His 2024 head-of-safety appointment remains historical.
The State Department underwent reorganization. Do not infer an agency reporting line from a historical bureau source.

Ritualo's current acting role relies on October 2026 reporting and 2026 event biographies; an official 2025 signed compliance plan corroborates the title. State.gov search did not expose a current biography.
Noah Jaffe and Katherine Reid searches returned unrelated people with identical names. Do not attribute those people's AI posts to the BIS officials.
Malik's Chief Super Intelligence Officer title comes from current reporting; the official March 2026 appointment release uses Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer.
Fewer than three promising discovery URLs were located for: Noah Jaffe (1), John Sonderman (2), Katherine Reid (1), Jessica Curyto (2), Ted Suzman (2).

The official Defense historical roster supplies CDAO dates. Search retrieval returned its text; direct retrieval returned HTTP 403.
The DOJ SI Task Force is distinct from the White House SI Force. Its October 13 memorandum merges the January 9 DOJ AI Task Force into it.

Several profiles have one or two useful sources after focused searches. Role-only pages and interviews after federal service carry explicit notes; they must not count as verified personal policy evidence.
